summary: Nobuyuki Kaji is a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. He held teaching posts at Koyasan, Tamkang, and Osaka universities, later serving as president of Koshien Junior College and professor at Ritsumeikan University.

Nobuyuki Watase is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his master's degree at Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor at Tokai University and later as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University.

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Genjun Sasaki. He held positions at Otani University and served as director of the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute.
Nora Kershaw Chadwick was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Newnham College from around 1911 to 1915. She later held posts at the University of St Andrews and the University of Cambridge.

Norbert Max Samuelson was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned degrees from Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He held major professorships at Temple University and Arizona State University.

Noriaki Hakamaya is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Komazawa Junior College, Komazawa University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
Noriaki Hosoda is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant and later as an associate professor at Hokkaido University.
Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from around 1949 to 1953 and later served there as a professor.

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku, Bukkyo, and Visva-Bharati universities. He spent his academic career at Bukkyo University, serving as lecturer, associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus.
Norihiko Uchida is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held an assistant post at Osaka University of Foreign Studies.

Norihisa Baba is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He holds a professorship at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Norio Koyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University.

Noritoshi Aramaki is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who earned doctorates from Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Osaka University and Otani University, and held posts at Kyoto University and Kyoto Koka Women's University.

Noriyuki Kudo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University. He has held teaching posts at Bukkyo University and Soka University's International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.

Norman Fischer is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Colgate University, University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Graduate Theological Union, and trained under Sojun Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. He founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.
Norvin J. Hein was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as an associate professor of comparative religion at Yale Divinity School.

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He served as associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions and held a post at the University of Oslo from 1986 to 2011.

Noémie Verdon is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand. She held a post attested at Kyoto University in 2019.

Noël Péri was a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Western music at Tokyo Music School before holding posts as resident and secretary-librarian at École Française d'Extrême-Orient. He also founded Mélanges japonais in 1904.
Nyanabodhi is a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied under the traditional teacher Ayya Khema and subsequently succeeded her.
